_readme: Trades are hand-edited ideas + script-evaluated status. SLATE model: up to one active idea per coin (max 5), listed in slate.coins[coin] = {trade_id | null, note}. Fields: id, coin, direction long|short, leverage (1-10 per idea; plus conviction low|medium|high and leverage_reason), entry (planned; replaced by fill price when filled, original kept in planned_entry), entry_zone {low, high} (optional), stop, targets[], opened_at, expiry (fill deadline for pending; legacy fill_by also accepted), expires (optional max hold for open trades), status pending|open|won|lost|stopped|cancelled (this public file shows closed ideas as status "closed" without exit price, P&L or targets hit; the full doc is private), missed_it {max_entry, note}, reasoning. Script fills targets_hit/filled_at/closed_at/exit_price/pnl_pct/unrealized_pnl_pct/mark_price (closed ideas: kept privately only). Hand edits of this file are merged by scripts/track_trades.py (load_trades). Times are ISO-8601; no offset = US Central.

slate.rules: Max one active (pending/open) idea per coin, max 6 at once; long or short; 'no setup' is allowed. Leverage is per idea, 1x-10x by conviction (low 1-2x, medium 3-5x, high 6-10x), capped so the loss at the stop from the worst fill is <= ~25% of margin; XDC is spot 1x.

Floor-to-ceiling legs have run +21-32% and ceiling-to-floor drops -15-20%, usually in 1-4 days. Price (~0.0545) sits just above the shelf, below mid-channel (~0.056), so this is a pending limit at the shelf, not a chase. Stop 0.0505 is under the 0.0516 shelf low: a break there means the October floor failed and price likely rotates to 0.0475-0.050 (a stop under 0.0475 from a 0.053 fill would risk about 35% of margin at 3x for a sub-1.5 R:R to T2). T1 0.0583 sits under the 0.0581-0.0591 lower-high cluster; T2 0.0620 sits under the 0.0625-0.0647 rejection wicks. R:R from the worst fill (0.0530): 2.1 to T1, 3.6 to T2. Signals: 1h Buy, 1d Buy (above EMA50/EMA200, daily StochRSI oversold), 4h Sell (below EMA20/50), so wait for the floor. Context: CoinDCX (Oct 15) reports the Oct 14 spike came with no Axelar announcement, on volume equal to 78% of market cap, and warns of sharp retracements once volume normalizes. That fits wick-and-fade range behaviour more than a breakout. Mirror trade: after T2, a rejection at 0.0615-0.0645 is the short back toward the shelf.
